sentences.text: The said Court after evidence was led, directed a payment of sum of Rs.3,500/- per month as maintenance to petitioner No.1 - wife till her life.
Rs.2,000/- per month to petitioner No.2 - daughter till her marriage and Rs.2,000/- per month to petitioner No.3 - Son, until he attains the majority.

4. Challenging the same, petitioner - husband had filed Criminal Revision Petition No.5151/2016 before the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangalore, Sitting at Puttur, D.K., which came to be dismissed by an order dated 22.01.2018.

sentences.text: Challenging the same, the petitioner - husband is before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner No.1 - wife, who is respondent No.1 herein is living a life of adultery as such, she is not entitled for any maintenance.

In so far as petitioner No.2 - Daughter, who is respondent No.2 herein, he submits that respondent No.2 having attained majority, there is no provision under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. to make payment of maintenance to a son or daughter, who has attained majority.

On these grounds, he submits that the above petition is required to be allowed and orders impugned are required to be set aside.
6.

Learned counsel for respondent would however submit that the contention of the alleged adultery has now been for the first time taken in the Criminal R.P. No.5151/2016 but no such contention had been taken up in Crl.Misc. No.24/2012.
In fact, it was the wife, who was taken up such contention against the petitioner - husband, which has been accepted by the trial Court.
The petitioner has also been convicted NC: 2024:KHC:10045 for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
Though the same has ended in a compromise subsequently, it is required for the petitioner to make payment of the maintenance amount as directed by the trial Court.

7. Heard Sri. P.B. Umesh, learned counsel for Sri. R. B. Deshpande, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri. B. V. Hemalath, learned counsel for Sri. B. R. Srinivasa Gowda, learned counsel appearing for respondents.
Perused the records.
8. The contention which has been urged in the present matter is firstly that the respondent No.1 - wife is living a life of adultery.
Secondly that respondent No.2 - daughter has attained majority.
Therefore, there is no requirement of payment of maintenance.

9. In so far as the first contention that the wife is living a life of adultery, there is no evidence which has been placed on record even before the trial Court or NC: 2024:KHC:10045 the revisional Court except to make vague statement and submissions in that regard.
The revisional Court has categorically come to the conclusion that there is nothing which has been placed on record to support the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner.
10. In fact in the present case also, there is nothing which has been placed on record to establish the alleged adulterous life that is led by the wife.

That being the case, I am of the opinion that the allegations alleged are completely hogwash only to get over the responsibility and liability of making Krishna Naika vs Smt Lalitha @ Shobha on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171101749/

sentences.text: 3 payment of maintenance amount to his wife, which is completely unsustainable and as such rejected.

11. In so far as the contention that respondent No.2 - daughter has attained majority, no order could have been passed by the trial Court for grant of maintenance till her marriage but it ought to have NC: 2024:KHC:10045 been restricted only till daughter attains majority.

Section 125 of Cr.P.C. reads as under:
"Section 125 - Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents 1) If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain.-
a) his wife, unable to maintain herself, or b) his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, whether married or not, unable to maintain itself, or c) his legitimate or illegitimate child (not being a married daughter) who has attained majority, where such child is, by reason of any physical or mental abnormality or injury unable to maintain itself,"
12. Section 125(1)(c ) provides for the legitimate or illegitimate child (not being a married daughter)
who has attained majority, where such child is, by reason of any physical or mental abnormality or injury unable to maintain itself.
Thus, in terms of Section 125(1)(c ) firstly, a married daughter is excluded.
Secondly, a child who has attained majority is also excluded subject however where such child is by reason of any physical or mental abnormality or injury is unable to maintain itself.

Hence, a son or daughter, who has attained majority, if not suffering from any physical or mental abnormality or injury NC: 2024:KHC:10045 resulting in a situation of such daughter or son being unable to maintain himself or herself, no maintenance can be awarded under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
13.

In the present case, the daughter having attained majority, the trial Court could not have directed making payment of any maintenance amount to such a daughter, who has attained majority, when she has not suffered any physical or mental abnormality or injury, which came in the way of maintaining herself, in that view of the matter in so far as the maintenance amount awarded to respondent No.2 - daughter is concerned, the order passed by the trial Court is contrary to the requirements of Section 125(1)(c ) of Cr.P.C. and is therefore required to be set aside.

14. General Observation:
The aspect of whether a child has attained majority has paled into insignificance in recent times when at NC: 2024:KHC:10045 the age of 18, most children would not have completed their education.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Education being a part of right to life and Article 21 as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court it cannot be expected of such a child be it either a son or daughter to stop their education and support himself or herself on attaining majority thereby, coming in the way of the future development of such child.

16. The exception which is been made over in Section 125(1)(c ) of Cr.P.C. requiring the father to make payment of maintenance amount to a child only if such child suffers from physical or mental abnormality or injury making a child unable to maintain itself, is in my opinion, a condition which comes in the way of the proper development of a child, who does not suffer from such abnormality and for the child to achieve its potential.

It would therefore be required for the Law Commission to look into this aspect and makes suitable amendments to Section 125(1)(c ) of Cr.P.C. so as to remove such restriction and make a parent liable for payment of maintenance amount be it either the father or mother, who is better placed than the other spouse to make payment of maintenance amount to a child until the child completes education and not restricted to the age of majority.

18. In view of the above discussion, I pass the following:
ORDER a.
Criminal petition is partly allowed.

b. The order dated 12.08.2016 passed by the Civil Judge and JMFC, Sullia, D.K. in Crl.Misc. No.24/2012 in so far as the maintenance awarded to respondent No.2 - daughter, based on her attaining majority, is set aside.
c. The petitioner - husband shall continue to make payment of maintenance amount to respondent No.1 - wife as directed in Crl.Misc. No.24/2012.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:10045 d.
The Registrar (Judicial) to forward a copy of this order to the Law Commission, Union of India for information.
